correctness.rationale: On an n>=4 tree, the sum of effective resistances is (1/n)sum_e b_e/g_e with b_e=k_e(n-k_e). Cauchy-Schwarz yields unique positive optimal g_e=B/S sqrt(b_e/c_e). The pseudoinverse voltage for a chord e_u-e_v is a sum of centered nested cut indicators divided by path conductances; their pairwise inner products min(s_i,s_j)(n-max(s_i,s_j))/n give exactly the displayed Theta_uv mixed-root expression. Trace-inverse on positive connected Laplacians is strictly convex along any nonzero simple-edge conductance perturbation. KKT at the tree-only candidate yields the simultaneous necessary-and-sufficient inequalities p_uv>=Theta_uv with equality included; subthreshold chord admits a budget-preserving improving perturbation. Independently simplified P4 unit-edge threshold 11/3+4/sqrt(3). Script exact-rational calculation inspected; its finite tests not substituted for all-tree argument.

value.rationale: A natural network design question is when a priced spanning tree remains optimal despite optional chords. The theorem gives a complete closed-form all-chord no-entry phase region from tree split sizes and costs, independent of budget, for all trees and heterogeneous prices; it avoids resolving the full convex allocation whenever candidate prices vary. The nested-cut mixed terms make long-path interactions explicit. This remains worthwhile even though the generic KKT method is established.
